calls.head: Turnovers could swing this one
calls.body: The Hurricanes turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Capitals are the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Capitals.
calls.call: The Hurricanes get at least their usual 7.9% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: Carolina 3rd for chances off turnovers (7.9% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Washington 32nd for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: 4.2% of Carolina’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.9%.

calls.head: The Hurricanes give up good looks, and the Capitals take them
calls.body: The Hurricanes have struggled to prevent dangerous shots, and the Capitals don’t waste many.
calls.call: The Capitals’ average shot has at least their usual 6.4% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Washington 10th for shot quality (a 6.4% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Carolina 32nd for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: Washington’s average shot had a 9.5% chance of going in, against their usual 6.4%.
calls.beyond: Washington’s shots at 5-on-5 were more dangerous than usual: a 9.5% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

calls.head: The Capitals get in close; the Hurricanes shoot from distance
calls.body: On shots from in close, Washington is near the top of the league and Carolina is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Capitals take a bigger share of their shots from within 20 feet than the Hurricanes.
calls.nums: Shots from in close: Washington 6th, Carolina 31st
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shots from within 20 feet, Washington had 38% and Carolina 34%. Coming in, Washington was at 31% and Carolina at 28%.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 73% chance, but Washington had other ideas.

WSH.head: We gave Washington a 27% chance, and Washington proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Washington leaned on their bottom six
surprises.body: Washington’s bottom-six forwards played 47% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 41% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

surprises.head: A rough night for B. Bussi
surprises.body: B. Bussi allowed 5 goals on shots worth 3.3 expected goals, 1.7 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 8 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: The Capitals beat the Hurricanes
paras: The Capitals had this one put away early. Alex Tuch scored twice, opening the scoring early in the first. Four different Capitals scored.
The chances were closer than the score.

items.text: Two of the preview’s three calls held.
